None of the SDD kind. Context m: whole source files named by the model, shown verbatim, plus short grep evidence spans (definitions, callers, strings) from up to 8 other files, under span headers; patch as unified diff (or search/replace in a control). Not specifications

CQ2-CARE (Algorithm 1): (1) path inventory ranked by word overlap with the issue; (2) localize: model gives independent ranked answers to "which files must change?" (5 drawn, L0-L2 used); keep files named by both L1 and L2 (fallback L0), excluding tests/docs; (3) plan up to 4 typed searches; grep evidence spans; (4) assemble context (files cut at 60K, evidence 12K, total <=80K tokens); (5) one patch call; (6) grading with benchmark tests

fields.why: The draft's works/partly/does-not-work verdicts rested on the extractor's own cut-offs (e.g. 43.7% 'works', 37.3% 'partly'); the authors state no success threshold for a configuration, so they are removed (author's rule of 2026-11-23). Per-configuration API cost from Table 16 added. The only stated criterion is H4 (non-inferiority of CQ2-CARE to another configuration), recorded as values; whether it counts as a per-configuration criterion is a judgement.

fields.v: 300 SWE-rebench issues (hash-drawn, eligibility checked: gold resolves, empty does not). Configurations: 9 context steps + oracle + no-source x 2 models. Baseline: compressors and retrievers (drop-in, no training) plus 2 trained methods added post hoc. Held constant: model per run, prompt byte-identical except context, per-issue token budget Bi (+-2% for compressors), post-processing, grader; repository names masked. Acceptance: benchmark FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests. Repetitions: one patch sample per cell (second sample for some controls). Human intervention: none. Planned hypotheses H1-H4 from an unfrozen written plan; several analyses post hoc

CQ2-CARE best: +6.3 pts over best compressor with both models (GPT: LongCodeZip 37.3; Claude: LLMLingua-2 40.3), +9.3 / +12.7 over best drop-in retriever; leads SweRank by 0.7 / 1.7 (n.s.) and SWE-Pruner by 2.0 (n.s.) / 7.3 (p < 0.05). Significant (one-sided exact McNemar, Holm) for all drop-in baselines, narrowest LLMLingua-2 with Claude p = 0.027. Gold files +5.7 with GPT, none with Claude. Cheaper: 0.68x tokens of single draw, non-inferior (ratio 0.94, lower bound 0.878)

Distinguished most configurations (not SweRank or SWE-Pruner with GPT). Repeatability: a second patch sample flips 8.7-18.9% of outcomes, so small gaps are fragile; CQ2-CARE still leads when both samples are averaged (p <= 0.002). Robustness checks (in-tolerance subset, search/replace format, 25/50/75% rates) keep the ordering. Limitations stated: comparison at CQ2-CARE's operating point; post-hoc additions; one patch call, not a multi-turn agent; exit-code grading would have been invalid (Appendix C)

One patch call per context on Python issues from one benchmark, not a multi-turn agent that can re-read files or run tests; budget fixed at CQ2-CARE's realized size; file-level BM25, controlled tests, SWE-Pruner and SweRank added post hoc; SweRank may have trained on PRs from the same repositories; most cells have one patch sample; possible training-data contamination and repositories seen during development; whether a selector beats a code-aware compressor starting from the same files is not shown. Future: full agent loop measuring re-reads
